review_method: External Stage 2 (Gemini bias) + Stage 3 (ChatGPT fact) run by operator and returned. Stage 6 self-verified the new lead figures (52.9% 2024) against primary/ministerial sources.
headline_finding: The central statistic was STALE. The issue was built on rice SSR 56.2% (2023); DOSM's 2020-2024 SUA (released 15 Dec 2025) reports 52.9% for 2024. This STRENGTHENS the story: the rate is falling, not flat. Restructured the whole issue around the verified decline.

changes.from: Raised target to 80% from 75%; actual rate 56.2%; gap 24 points 'not narrowing'.
changes.to: Targets 80% by 2030 (DAN 2.0, 75% interim); rate FELL to 52.9% in 2024 from 56.2% in 2023; gap ~27 points.
changes.reason: Stage 3: 56.2% is the 2023 figure; latest DOSM (15 Dec 2025) reports 52.9% for 2024. Self-verified: confirmed across DOSM PDF existence + The Star (5 Feb 2026, Minister Mat Sabu calls it 'stagnant at 52%') + multiple outlets. Leading with the decline is both accurate and a stronger story.

changes.from: 'It has been broadly flat.' / 'gap nearly 24 points'
changes.to: 'sliding: 56.2% in 2023, then 52.9% in 2024 ... longer fall from about 70% in 2017' / 'gap is now about 27 points'
changes.reason: Both reviewers: 'broadly flat' UNDERCLAIMS a real decline. MyCC 2026 public report traces ~70% (2017) -> 56.2% (2023); DOSM 52.9% (2024). Reframed as a decline with the MyCC long-arc attribution.

changes.from: 'raised its rice self-sufficiency target to 80% by 2030, up from the previous 75%'
changes.to: 'targets 80% rice self-sufficiency by 2030, with a 75% interim mark' (DAN 2.0)
changes.reason: Both reviewers: the 75%/80% are phased DAN 2.0 (2021-2030) milestones (75% interim, 80% by 2030), not a target that was 'raised'. Removed the false policy-shift implication.

changes.from: 'not the net food trade deficit of about RM31 billion. Both widened as the ringgit weakened.'
changes.to: 'Food exports trailed at RM46.5 billion that year, leaving a food trade deficit of RM32.3 billion.'
changes.reason: Stage 3: the ~RM31B deficit is 2022, paired with the 2023 import bill (year-mismatch); the 2023 deficit is RM32.3B (imports RM78.8B - exports RM46.5B, DOSM). Also dropped 'ringgit weakened' as an unsupported causal OVERCLAIM.
Stage 3: 100 - SSR is the self-sufficiency gap, not the exact import share; 'nearly half' is defensible against both the 2023 and 2024 SSR without overprecision.

changes.to: 'banned non-basmati white rice exports in July 2023'
changes.reason: Stage 3: precise wording per DGFT Notification 20/2023 (20 July 2023).

changes.from: 'A government can legislate a target but not a harvest. Rice security is won in the granary, not the gazette.'
changes.to: 'A government can set a target but not guarantee a harvest. Rice security is decided in the paddy field, not the policy document.'
changes.reason: Stage 3: 'legislate/gazette' implies a statutory/gazetted target; it is a policy target under DAN 2.0. Removed the false legal framing while keeping the kicker.

rejected_or_held_flags.reason: Stage 3 marked this UNVERIFIED (could not confirm the exact FAO-alignment, clean-padi, or 4.7% figure from primary). Per the Accuracy Standard, kept entirely out of the cards. The decline framing (56.2% -> 52.9%) does not depend on it. Note: this resolves the Stage 2 'apples-to-oranges' concern differently than Stage 2 proposed (Stage 2 wanted the methodology IN the text; Stage 3 says it is unverifiable) -- by leading with the same-methodology 2023->2024 decline, the comparison is now like-for-like and the methodology caveat is unnecessary.

scores.ba_note: 100 - bias_score(5); near-zero bias, no partisan/communal/gender framing.
scores.fc_note: Stage 3 score as returned; reflects the stale-figure and framing errors found at review time. Corrected (incl. self-verified 52.9%), not re-inflated.

chart: Regenerated issue-2003-bg.png: now shows the 52.9% (2024) actual and the falling trend vs the 80% target, replacing the stale 56.2%/24-point version.
